title: 🎵 VIBE CODING
subtitle: with Claude Code Extension

banner: 🤖 Copy-Paste AI Prompts for Every Task

content.value: Vibe Coding is a revolutionary development philosophy that transforms how developers collaborate with AI coding assistants. Instead of treating AI as a simple autocomplete tool, Vibe Coding establishes a structured workflow where AI understands your project's architecture, design system, and coding standards.
The term 'Vibe' comes from finding a natural rhythm between human intent and AI execution. When the vibe is right, code flows naturally, consistently, and with minimal friction.
🎵 VIBE: The Core Philosophy — You are the architect, AI is your skilled assistant. You define what to build, AI helps you build it consistently.
Vibe Coding is built on three fundamental principles:

items: Context-First Development: Establish rich context through @file references
Rules-Based Consistency: CLAUDE.md defines AI behavior standards
Plan-First Implementation: Always request a plan before code generation

content.value: ✅ BEST PRACTICE: Teams using Vibe Coding report 40% faster code reviews and 60% fewer design system violations.
The @file command is the most powerful tool in Vibe Coding. It tells Claude Code to include a file's complete content as context for any request.

content.title: Your First @file Prompt
content.prompt: @file src/components/Card.tsx - Create a new UserCard component that follows the same styling patterns
content.tip: AI will read Card.tsx and replicate its structure, styling, and patterns automatically.

content.value: ⚠️ WARNING: Never describe patterns in words when you can show them with @file. Showing beats telling every time.
Every feature follows a structured workflow from requirements to deployment:

content.title: Request Implementation Plan
content.prompt: @file src/features/UserProfile.tsx @file src/types/user.ts - Plan a new NotificationSettings feature following the same patterns. Include: component structure, state management, API integration, and test strategy.
content.tip: Always request a plan BEFORE any code generation. Review it, adjust, then approve.
